title: Template-driven Forms
summary: Build forms right in the template with ngModel — great for simple forms.
heading: Template-driven Forms

blocks.text: Angular gives you two styles of forms. They do the same job — collect and validate user input — but put the logic in different places.

layers.title: Template-driven
layers.detail: Form logic lives in the template with ngModel. Simple and quick — this chapter.

layers.title: Reactive
layers.detail: Form model lives in the TypeScript class. More powerful for big or dynamic forms — next chapter.

blocks.text: Reach for template-driven forms for small things like a login or contact form. Reach for reactive forms when the form is large, dynamic, or needs serious validation and testing.
Template-driven forms come from FormsModule. Add it to the component's imports.

blocks.label: component

blocks.text: Each input uses [(ngModel)] for two-way binding and a name attribute so the form can track it. Wrap the inputs in a <form> and handle (ngSubmit).

blocks.label: signup.html
blocks.code:
<form (ngSubmit)="submit()">
  <input name="name" [(ngModel)]="model.name" placeholder="Name">
  <input name="email" [(ngModel)]="model.email" placeholder="Email">
  <button type="submit">Sign up</button>
</form>

blocks.text: Add normal HTML validators like required and minlength. Give the input a template reference (#name="ngModel") to read its state and show messages.

blocks.label: signup.html
blocks.code:
<input
  name="name"
  [(ngModel)]="model.name"
  required
  minlength="3"
  #name="ngModel">

@if (name.invalid && name.touched) {
  <small>Name must be at least 3 characters.</small>
}

blocks.text: Useful states on a control: valid / invalid, touched (the user visited it), and dirty (the value changed).
Give the form a reference with #form="ngForm" to check if the entire form is valid — handy for disabling the submit button.

items: Template-driven forms keep the logic in the template; import FormsModule.
Bind inputs with [(ngModel)] and give each a name.
Validate with required, minlength, etc.; read state via #ref="ngModel".
Use #form="ngForm" for the whole form's validity.
